<!-- markdownlint-disable MD013 -->
# seakarr

Automated Soulseek music downloader with library quality upgrading.

## Features

- **Library quality scanner** — walks your music library directories, reads audio tags (FLAC, MP3, AAC,
  OGG, Opus, WAV, WMA, and more via [lofty](https://crates.io/crates/lofty)), and identifies albums
  whose tracks are in a format outside `filters.allowed_extensions` or fall below the
  configurable bitrate threshold.
- **Upgrade mode** — for each album needing an upgrade, searches the Soulseek network, ranks
  candidates by advertised speed (adjusted by measured-throughput reputation), free-slot bonus, bitrate bonus,
  album-name match and peer reliability, and downloads the best match. The result is written into your
  library when the artist already has a folder under a configured `library.paths` entry, and stays in
  `storage.staging_dir` when it does not; an album selected by `library_upgrade.enabled` is replaced in
  place. An upgrade whose every destination already holds a strictly better file
  keeps those files and still completes the album, so the staging copy is removed without a new file being
  written. A candidate whose files omit the bitrate attribute scores zero on the bitrate bonus once
  `filters.min_bit_rate` is set, so a peer that reports one is preferred; it is still admitted, because its
  real quality is verified after download.
- **Discover mode** — derives the artist list from your library (tags first,
  folder names as the fallback), keeps only the artists that own a folder of
  their own, asks MusicBrainz which conceptual albums each of those is missing,
  and downloads only those. An artist the library only knows as a guest inside
  another artist's folder is skipped, and the run summary reports how many were
  skipped that way; name one explicitly with `--artist` to process it anyway.
  Naming an artist explicitly does not require the library to hold an album for
  it: when a folder named after the artist exists, the artist is processed and
  its albums are placed into that folder, and when there is neither an album nor
  a folder the run warns and keeps the downloads in staging.
  Albums already present are never
  searched or re-downloaded, and each run stops after
  `discover.max_cycle_downloads` download attempts so a large library fills in
  over successive runs. Release types come from `discography.allowed_types`.
- **Manual & batch modes** — search for a specific artist/album on demand, or process a newline-separated
  text file of `artist - album` lines to download a curated wantlist.
  A run places each completed album into the artist's existing library folder when one exists
  anywhere under a configured `library.paths` entry; when the artist has no folder there, or the
  album's destination folder already exists, a manual run keeps the download in
  `storage.staging_dir` (batch and upgrade runs merge into the existing folder instead, keeping
  any file that already parses as audio). An
  album-only request names no artist, so it always stays in staging and says nothing: only manual
  mode can express one, because upgrade mode rejects `--album` on its own and a batch line is trimmed
  before it is parsed, so a line written as `" - Album"` is read as an artist-only line. An artist-naming run with a configured library path explains a
  staging-only download once it has one.
- **Authoritative artist discography** — artist-only manual runs resolve conceptual albums from MusicBrainz
  release groups (cached locally for 30 days) and then run one sequential `Artist Album` Soulseek search per
  eligible album, oldest first. The same authoritative resolution powers `discover` mode for every artist
  it sweeps — those that own a folder named after them. Release categories and optional MusicBrainz artist IDs are configurable; the
  previous folder heuristic remains the explicit opt-out and the visible fallback.
- **Quality filtering** — filter Soulseek results by file extension, minimum
  bitrate, excluded keywords, and upload availability. With
  `download.max_queue_length: 0` a peer must offer a free upload slot; a
  positive limit also admits zero-slot peers until their reported queue
  position can be validated. Path-traversal names are rejected.
- **Peer reputation** — remembers each peer's effective throughput (bytes ÷ transfer time: retry delays plus
  the final transfer, excluding queue wait) and success rate (in SQLite), and ranks search results by a blend
  of advertised and measured throughput plus a reliability factor, so fast, reliable peers are preferred and
  slow or error-prone peers are demoted — regardless of what you search for. Controlled by

## Phase 1 findings — Root Cause Investigation (investigation only; no edits, no fixes, no subagents)

### Symptom as reported
`--mode discover --artist X` walks the whole library first and asks MusicBrainz about the artist second, so the MusicBrainz verdict only arrives after the scan. If the artist is not on MusicBrainz, the scan time is spent for nothing.

### Traced data flow (exact sequence, current HEAD `171f65c` = v0.30.0)
1. `src/main.rs:235` `resolve_execution_plan` — cheap config validation only, no I/O: `discography.enabled`, ≥1 `library.paths` entry, `--album` incompatibility, non-blank `--artist` (`src/mode.rs:223-262`).
2. Soulseek connect/login, then `src/main.rs:365` `dispatch_execution_plan` → `runner::run_discover_mode` (`src/main.rs:583`).
3. `src/runner.rs:2253` `run_discover_mode` — re-checks the same two config preconditions, constructs `MusicBrainzProvider` (**no request is made**), delegates to `run_discover_mode_with_provider`.
4. `src/runner.rs:2418` `run_discover_mode_with_provider` — the ordering in question:
   - `2442` arm cancellation, `2446` progress display
   - **`2452` `scan_library_cancellable` → `scanner::scan_library`** (`src/runner.rs:104-131`, `src/scanner.rs:240`) — the full tag-reading walk over *every* `library.paths` root (lofty parses each file).
   - `2455` `discover::build_index(&scanned)`
   - `2463-2468` `ArtistFolderIndex::new(config).find(name)` — directory names only, lazy, reached only when the index lacks the name
   - `2469` `discover::select_artists(...)`
   - **`2530` first provider call** — `discover_artist_albums(provider, …)` → `src/discography/mod.rs:659/678`: cache lookup → `provider.search_artists()` → `resolve_artist()` (`mod.rs:196`) → `provider.release_groups()`.

### Root cause
`artist_filter` is **not read until `src/runner.rs:2463`**, i.e. after `scan_library_cancellable` has already returned at `2452`. Discover's work list is library-derived (`build_index` → `select_artists`), and the `--artist` narrowing is applied *inside* that selection rather than before it, so an explicitly named artist cannot short-circuit the scan. There is no pre-scan validation branch anywhere in the discover path — `rg` for preflight/validate/check_artist in `runner.rs` returns nothing.

The project itself documents the scan as the expensive part: `README.md:479` — *"The library scan is the longest silent phase of a run"*. Scan cost scales with library size and file count; MusicBrainz cost is bounded by the client's own pacing (1 req/s) and a 30-day discography cache.

### Working example already in the same repo (opposite order)
Manual artist-only mode does exactly what the user wants: `run_artist_only_mode_with_provider` (`src/runner.rs:1952`) calls `discover_artist_albums` at **1963**, then scans at **1985** (`discover::index_from_paths`, `src/discover.rs:835`) and filters with `missing_albums` at 2013. So "MusicBrainz first, scan second" is an existing, tested pattern in this codebase — discover mode is the outlier, not a missing capability.

### What actually happens today on each failure class
- **Unresolved** (`DiscoveryFailure::Unresolved`, `src/discography/mod.rs:572`): the run does not abort; it warns `"artist could not be resolved on MusicBrainz"`, increments the `unresolved` counter, downloads nothing, and exits **0**. Per `mod.rs:565-577`, `Unresolved` deliberately does not count toward the provider circuit breaker.
- Important nuance: `DiscographyError::ArtistUnresolved` is produced by **four** different causes (`resolve_artist`/`resolve_dominant_artist`, `mod.rs:196-290`): no exact-name candidate at all, a tied top score, a top score below the threshold, and a margin below the margin threshold. So "unresolved" currently means *"could not be confidently resolved"*, not strictly *"does not exist"*.
- **Provider outage**: consecutive-failure counter; the third consecutive failure aborts with `SeakarrError::MusicBrainz` (pinned by the test at `src/runner.rs:6557-6565`).
- **Caching**: for an explicit `--artist`, `failure_cache = FailureCacheUse::Bypass` (`src/runner.rs:2481-2483`), so a previously recorded resolution failure is deliberately ignored and the network lookup runs every time (test at `src/runner.rs:6645-6662` asserts `provider.calls() > 0`). A *fresh* discography cache (~30 days) does avoid the MusicBrainz request, but the library scan still happens first regardless.

### Recent change that shaped current behaviour
`git log -S 'only narrow to artists already present'` shows the old refusal was introduced in `dc3a9b5` and **removed in `3395e9e`** ("feat: fill in an artist folder that holds no albums in discover mode", v0.30.0). Today an unknown artist is a warning plus staging fallback, not an error — the pre-v0.30.0 hard refusal is gone. `3395e9e` also added the folder-evidence path (`ArtistFolderIndex::find` at `2463`) but left it *after* the scan.

### Reproduction status
- Code-level ordering is deterministic and single-threaded: `scan (2452) → select (2469) → provider (2530)`.
- Empirical: `cargo test --lib -- --nocapture --test-threads=1 discover_skips_an_unresolved_artist_without_searching discover_narrows_to_the_requested_artist discover_excludes_configured_artists_before_any_lookup` → **3 passed / 0 failed, exit 0** (`discover_skips_an_unresolved_artist_without_searching` uses a real temp library fixture, so the scan provably runs before the unresolvable verdict and still issues no Soulseek search).
- **Gap:** no test pins the scan-before-provider order, so the current sequence can be re-inverted silently — worth pinning when the order changes.
- End-to-end CLI reproduction was not attempted: it requires Soulseek credentials/network. The user's 2026-10-05 log shows the sequence in production: connect → `Library scan complete: 2114 audio file(s), 196 album(s) in 1.4s` → artist verdict.

### Scope finding (affects the fix's shape)
The reorder is only meaningful for the **explicit `--artist`** case. In the sweep (no `--artist`) the artist list *is* the scan output, so MusicBrainz cannot be consulted before the scan there.

Caveat to note in the wording: "unresolved" also covers ambiguous/tied matches, not only non-existence, so the message must say "could not be resolved on MusicBrainz" rather than "does not exist". Makes a scheduled/kiosk run fail loudly.

## Phase 1 complete — findings and recorded decisions

**Working tree verified clean** (`git status --porcelain` empty, HEAD `171f65c` = v0.30.0). Investigation only: no files read beyond source/docs, nothing edited, no subagents dispatched.

### Root cause (confirmed)
Discover mode applies `--artist` narrowing *after* the library scan, not before it. Concretely, `artist_filter` is not read until `src/runner.rs:2463`, whereas `scan_library_cancellable` (the full tag-reading walk) completes at `2452` and `select_artists` runs at `2469`; the first MusicBrainz call is at `2530`. Because discover's work list is derived from the scan (`build_index` → `select_artists`), no pre-scan artist validation exists anywhere in the path — so the MusicBrainz verdict can only ever arrive after the scan, and `README.md:479` names that scan as "the longest silent phase of a run".

The desired order already exists in the repo: artist-only manual mode resolves MusicBrainz at `1952/1963` and scans at `1985`. Discover is the outlier.

### Decisions recorded
| Decision | Choice |
| --- | --- |
| Fail-fast on an artist MusicBrainz cannot resolve (`--mode discover --artist X`) | **Hard error before any library scan**, non-zero exit, MusicBrainz-worded message |
| Structure of the pre-scan step | **Hoist and reuse** — resolve the named artist once, above the scan, and thread the result into the album loop; one MusicBrainz lookup per run (mirrors manual mode) |
| Recorded-failure cache for the named artist | **Keep bypassing** (`FailureCacheUse::Bypass`, `src/runner.rs:2481-2483`) |

### Scope boundary — verified against the code, matches your clarification
- `MusicBrainzProvider::new()` is constructed at exactly two sites: `src/runner.rs:2142` (artist-only manual) and `2270` (discover). Nothing else touches MusicBrainz.
- Manual mode with `--album` never reaches either: `run_manual_mode` only enters the artist-only/MusicBrainz branch when `album.is_none()` (`2725` goes straight to `process_album`). So there is no MusicBrainz hard-error surface in that path to protect.
- The new hard error is therefore confined to **discover mode with an explicit `--artist`**. Untouched: discover's automatic sweep (its artist list *is* the scan output, so it cannot be reordered), and artist-only manual mode's existing fallback behaviour on both unresolved and provider failure.
- Wording constraint carried from the investigation: `ArtistUnresolved` covers four causes (no exact-name candidate, tied top score, score below threshold, margin below threshold), so the message must say "could not be resolved on MusicBrainz" — never "does not exist".

### Open assumption for the fix step (flagging rather than re-asking)
A MusicBrainz **outage** (`DiscoveryFailure::Provider`) is not an "artist does not exist" verdict. I intend the same ordering rule to apply — stop before the scan, with an outage-specific message — while leaving the existing 3-consecutive-failure circuit breaker semantics (`src/runner.rs:6557-6565`) intact. Say the word if you want an outage to behave differently.

### What a RED test should pin
No test currently pins scan-before-provider ordering, so it can be silently re-inverted. The failing test should assert, with a mock provider and an unresolvable named artist, that **the provider was consulted and the library walk was never entered** (and that a resolvable named artist still scans exactly once), plus the readable-contrast case: artist-only manual mode with an unresolvable artist still falls back to the legacy heuristic and does **not** hard-error.

771:### Discover mode

### Discover mode

Fills in what an existing library is missing. Seakarr walks `library.paths` once and derives
the artist list from tags where present, falling back to folder names, keeping only the artists
that own a folder named after them. Each swept artist is resolved
on MusicBrainz using the same authoritative resolution as artist-only manual mode, and the
release groups in `discography.allowed_types` are the only candidates. Albums already present
in the library are skipped, and the remainder runs through the same search, ranking,
download, placement, and notification pipeline as the other modes, oldest album first.
`discover.exclude_artists` skips aggregator names before any lookup, the
folder-ownership gate keeps an artist the library knows only as a guest inside
another artist's folder out of the sweep, `--artist` optionally
names one artist to process on its own (overriding both
the exclusion list and the gate), whether or not the library holds an album for
it — a folder named after it is the destination, and with neither album nor
folder the downloads stay in staging — and the run stops after
`discover.max_cycle_downloads` download attempts so a large library fills in over successive
runs.

Each completed album is placed in the artist's own library folder — the directory that artist's
existing albums were scanned from, or, for an explicitly named artist the library holds no album
for, the folder a name lookup found — as `<artist folder>/<album title>/NN - Title.ext`, with the artist
folder named exactly as it is on disk and the album folder named from the MusicBrainz title. Placement
is unconditional in discover mode: it does not depend on
`library_upgrade.enabled`, and `library_upgrade.delete_lesser_quality` never applies to it. Once the
copy succeeds the staging directory for that album is removed, so discover leaves nothing behind.
The scanner resolves the artist folder, album folder, and library location positionally and steps
over one dedicated disc folder (`CD 01`, `Disc 2`), so nested layouts such as
`<root>/Genre/Artist/Album` and albums whose discs sit in dedicated disc folders place correctly. The
album folder must hold the files itself: for an untagged `<root>/Artist/Album/FLAC/01.flac` the
sub-folder is read as the album (`Album` becomes the artist and `FLAC` the album), so keep format or
extra sub-folders outside the album folder.
An album split across marker-shaped folders (`Gold (Disc 1)/`, `Gold (Disc 2)/` under one album
folder) reads as two albums and is documented as a limit rather than corrected; the derived artist
folder is then the marker folder's parent (`Gold/`), which also feeds the discover destination pair
when those are the artist's only albums. Such an artist owns no folder named after the tag
spelling, so the folder gate keeps it out of an automatic sweep; `--artist` processes it. A placed
album that keeps a marker folder is therefore
indexed under the marker name, not the album title, so a later run with a cleared database or
`--ignore-processed` can download it again. On the upgrade path the same shape can also nest one
level too deep, giving `<artist>/Gold (Disc 1)/Gold (Disc 1)/...`, because the disc folder is
preserved under an album whose own name is that marker. A manual run places albums into the
artist's existing library folder and never creates one: with no folder for the artist the download
stays in `staging_dir`.

## Data flow

1. `scan_library(library.paths, filters, cancel)` walks the library once,
   returning `Cancelled` if the cancellation flag is set, and reporting its
   progress (start, per-minute heartbeat, per-500-file debug line, unreadable
   count, completion).
2. `build_index` turns the scanned albums into the presence index.
3. `select_artists` applies exclusions, the folder-ownership gate and the
   optional filter, and orders the result.
4. For each artist, while the budget is not exhausted:

   a. `discover_artist_albums(provider, db, artist, discography_config)`
      returns authoritative albums from a fresh cache, the network, or a stale
      cache, or reports the artist as unresolvable or failed.
   b. `missing_albums` removes every album already present.
   c. For each remaining album, oldest first: run `process_album`, which
      searches, ranks, downloads, organises, and notifies exactly as it does
      elsewhere, and charge the budget when the outcome is `Downloaded` or
      `Failed` — the two outcomes that reached the download stage.

5. Aggregate counts are added to the run report as notices, and the summary is
   printed once.

## TDD step complete — RED → GREEN → REFACTOR

Prerequisites preserved (`Harness status: loaded.`, `Project context status: loaded.`). No subagents dispatched at any point.

### RED — failing tests written first, before any production code
Five tests added (`src/runner.rs`), then run against unchanged production code. Three failed for exactly the expected reasons; the two guards passed by design (they pin behaviour that must *not* change).

| Test | What it pins | RED result (before the fix) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `discover_hard_errors_on_an_unresolvable_named_artist_before_scanning_the_library` | Named artist MB cannot resolve → `Config` error naming the artist, no walk, no Soulseek search | FAILED — `got Scanner("library path does not exist: …")`, i.e. the walk had already run |
| `discover_verifies_a_named_artist_before_it_scans_the_library` | Ordering on the success path: MB answers (`calls() == 1`) before the walk is attempted | FAILED — `provider.calls()` left `0`, right `1` |
| `discover_stops_before_the_scan_when_musicbrainz_is_unavailable` | Provider outage → warn + stop before the walk (exit 0), never a hard error | FAILED — `Err(Scanner("library path does not exist: …"))` |
| `discover_resolves_a_named_artist_once_and_fills_its_gap` (guard) | One name costs exactly one provider dialog | passed (guard) |
| `manual_artist_only_mode_does_not_hard_error_on_an_unresolvable_artist` (guard) | Your constraint: manual mode keeps its heuristic fallback, no MusicBrainz hard error | passed (guard) |

The decisive technique: the "did the walk run?" observation uses a **non-existent library root**, which makes `scanner::scan_library` fail with `SeakarrError::Scanner`. Any run that walks first is therefore detectable from the error variant and from `provider.calls()` — no mocks of the scanner, no instrumentation of production code.

### GREEN — minimal implementation
- `run_discover_mode_with_provider` now resolves an explicitly named artist **before** `scan_library_cancellable`: `verify_named_artist` → `discover_artist_albums(..., FailureCacheUse::Bypass)`.
- Unresolved → `SeakarrError::Config("artist \"X\" could not be resolved on MusicBrainz (…); discover mode needs a verified artist to build its work list")`, raised before the walk (wording deliberately never says "does not exist", since `ArtistUnresolved` also covers ambiguity/tied scores).
- Provider outage → existing breaker bookkeeping, warn `"<name>: MusicBrainz unavailable (<reason>); artist skipped"`, summary printed, run stops before the walk (exit 0). Your "keep bypassing" decision is preserved.
- The resolved outcome is **reused** as the artist's work list in the loop, so a named artist still costs exactly one MusicBrainz dialog. The automatic sweep is untouched — its artist list *is* the walk's output.

### REFACTOR (tests stayed green throughout)
- Extracted `finish_discover_run` and reused it in the loop tail and `abort_discover_run`, so the pre-walk stop reports through the same path as a full run.
- Extracted `note_provider_failure` (warn + counter + breaker) and used it in **both** the pre-walk path and the sweep loop, so an outage observed before the walk counts towards the same circuit breaker and the two call sites cannot drift.
- Collapsed a three-state enum to two (`WorkList` / `Stop`) and folded the caller's double `match` into one; corrected two doc comments that no longer described the code.

### One existing test updated (intentional expectation change)
`an_explicit_artist_bypasses_a_recorded_failure` asserted a silent `Ok` for an explicit artist with a recorded failure and an unresolvable provider — precisely the behaviour you asked to change. Its original intent (the recorded row must not stand in for the lookup) is preserved and strengthened: it now asserts `provider.calls() == 1` **and** the fatal `Config` verdict, which is what distinguishes a bypassed lookup from a replayed skip.

- `README.md` — Discover mode now states the named-artist verification order, the hard error, the outage stop, and that the sweep keeps scan-first; the `--artist` row gained the same clause.

Discover mode with an explicit `--artist` is the only path that changed in behaviour. Verified by construction and by guards: the sweep still warns and continues on an unresolved artist (`discover_skips_an_unresolved_artist_without_searching`, `an_unresolvable_artist_is_not_an_outage_…`), and manual mode — including the `--album` path, which never constructs a `MusicBrainzProvider` — still falls back heuristically.

The `Config` error propagates through `?` at runner.rs:2586; the `Stop` arm returns `Ok(())` at runner.rs:2585; no path re-enters the walk after a `Stop`.
- **No double-reporting.** `finish_discover_run` (runner.rs:2232-2244) is called exactly once per run: inside `verify_named_artist` for the outage `Stop` (runner.rs:2319), inside `abort_discover_run` for a breaker abort (runner.rs:2253), and once at the end of the loop (runner.rs:2777). The outage path prints the summary *before* returning, and the caller does not print again.
- **Outcome reuse cannot be applied to the wrong artist.** With a non-blank filter, `select_artists` (discover.rs:520-585) either early-returns exactly one artist (folder or staging branch) or keeps only the index key equal to `filter_key`; the pre-resolved name and the selected `artist.name` always share one `normalize_catalog_key` (index branch: same key; folder branch: `ArtistFolderIndex::find` matches on `normalize_catalog_key(sanitize_component(...))`, discover.rs:265-267 + 300-312, and the pre-resolve keys the cache by `normalize_catalog_key(filter)`), and `contains_album`/`missing_albums` key the artist the same way (discover.rs:137, 182-186). A dropped `pre_resolved` (empty selection) is unreachable for a non-blank filter because `has_artist` ⇒ `filter_key ∈ artist_keys` and every index entry has ≥1 spelling (discover.rs:414).
- **Breaker bookkeeping is shared correctly.** `note_provider_failure` (runner.rs:2406-2421) increments once, warns once, records `(artist, reason)`, and reaches the abort before the summary is printed twice; the stale-cache path is *not* double-counted because `verify_named_artist` deliberately lets the loop's `note_stale_cache` (runner.rs:2686-2699) do the counting for a reused stale outcome. The abort arm in `verify_named_artist` is unreachable in production (limit 3, one pre-walk call, fresh counter) and is honestly disclosed as seeded by the test at runner.rs:7852-7860 — defensive, not a defect.
- **`counters.artists_total = 1` in the outage path is the right guard**: without it, `discover_notices` (discover.rs:747-752) would add "no eligible library artists found; nothing to do" beside the provider-failed notice. `artists_total` is re-derived from the selection in the success path (runner.rs:2633), so no double-count.
- **Docs generally match the code**: README:790-796 and the spec supersession note (spec:416-420) are accurate for the no-cache case; `Bypass` genuinely never replays (discography/mod.rs:883-886), so the updated `an_explicit_artist_bypasses_a_recorded_failure` (runner.rs:6815) correctly pins a live lookup (`calls() == 1`, would be 0 under a `Honour` regression).
- Test helpers are sound: `undiscoverable_library` (runner.rs:7688-7695) makes "did it walk?" observable via a `Scanner` error rather than a silent empty scan, which is what makes the ordering tests (runner.rs:7744, 7780) meaningful.

### Findings (all P2, report-only — no P0/P1 logic bugs found)

**P2-1 — `discover_resolves_a_named_artist_once_and_fills_its_gap` cannot detect the regression it names.**
runner.rs:7815-7850. The test claims to pin "the pre-scan answer is the run's work list", but with the fixture's `cache_days = 30` (config.rs:254-256 via `Config::default()`), the pre-resolve already wrote a fresh cache row (`upsert_discography_cache`, discography/mod.rs:770-775). A mutation that drops the reuse (loop always calls `discover_artist_albums`) would find `cache_is_fresh` true (discography/mod.rs:829-836), return `FreshCache`, issue **no** `search_artists` call, and produce the same search queries — so `provider.calls() == 1` and the query assertion still pass. Concrete failure: someone deletes `pre_resolved`/the `take()` at runner.rs:2671-2679 and every named-artist run silently pays a second resolution whenever the cache is stale or `discography.cache_days: 0` (where `cache_is_fresh` is always false); no test fails. Smallest fix: add `config.discography.cache_days = 0;` to this test (a re-query must then reach the provider, so `calls()` becomes 2 under the mutation and 1 with the reuse).

**P2-2 — The outage-stop summary's counter fix is untested.**
runner.rs:2310-2315 vs runner.rs:7780-7813. The only test for the outage-before-the-walk branch inspects the WARN log; it never asserts on the printed summary (which goes through `tracing::info!`, so `LogCapture` can see it — report.rs:160-164, test_support.rs:245). Deleting `counters.artists_total = 1` makes the outage run print `discover: no eligible library artists found; nothing to do` *and* `discover: provider failed for Outage Named Artist (...)` (discover.rs:747-752 and 800-805), and all six new tests stay green. Smallest fix: positively assert `logs.contains("provider failed for Outage Named Artist")` in that test (avoid a bare negative assertion: the capture window is open to concurrent non-capturing tests per test_support.rs:170-176).

**P2-3 — README/spec claim "an outage … stops before the walk" is unconditional; it is false when a usable cache exists.**
README.md:793-794, README.md:1011-1013, spec:416-420. A refresh failure with a compatible cache row returns `Authoritative`/`AuthoritativeEmpty` with `StaleCache` provenance (`stale_or_legacy`, discography/mod.rs:991-1010), which `verify_named_artist` returns as `WorkList` (runner.rs:2290-2294): the run *does* walk the library and proceeds on the stale albums (only a warning, via `note_stale_cache`, runner.rs:2686-2699). A fresh cache means no outage is even observed. Smallest fix: qualify with "when no usable cache exists" in README:794/1012 and spec:419-420.

**P2-4 — The spec's Error-handling contract still says an unresolved artist is skipped.**
spec:510-511: "**Artist unresolved by MusicBrainz** – skip and report; no broad Soulseek search and no legacy fallback." For an explicitly named discover artist that is now a fatal `Config` error with no skip and no report (runner.rs:2304-2307), contradicting the bullet. The file's convention is a dated `*(superseded …)*` annotation (e.g. spec:527-532). Smallest fix: append `*(superseded 2026-10-07 for an explicitly named discover artist: a `Config` error before the walk)*` to that bullet.

**P2-5 — Two comments now state the wrong MusicBrainz spelling for the folder-only case.**
The pre-walk lookup uses the typed/trimmed filter (runner.rs:2575 → 2286-2290), but the folder-only path hands the loop the *on-disk* folder spelling (discover.rs:529-535) and reuses the typed name's outcome. Concretely, the fixture at runner.rs:7913/7922 (`--artist "shy fx"`, folder `Shy Fx`) now sends `shy fx` to MusicBrainz, while discover.rs:540-542 and the test comment at runner.rs:7950 assert the on-disk spelling is what MusicBrainz is asked about. No functional harm (same normalized artist; search/placement still use the folder spelling), but the comments are false. Smallest fix: reword both to say the operator's typed name goes to MusicBrainz and the on-disk spelling drives search/placement (the folder name is unknowable before the walk, so it cannot be the query).

**P2-6 — Narrow edge case: a non-blank name that normalizes to the empty key now costs a provider call and reports the wrong error.**
runner.rs:2575 gates pre-resolution on `trim().is_empty()`, while `select_artists` rejects a filter whose *normalized* key is empty (discover.rs:522-536). With `--artist "'"` (or any string of apostrophe-like characters; `normalize_catalog_key` strips them, discography/mod.rs:48-72), the run first issues a MusicBrainz search and then reports `artist "'" could not be resolved on MusicBrainz (...)`, instead of the documented blank-name `Config` error ("Blank `--artist` – configuration error naming the artist", spec:530-531) and without the pointless lookup. Smallest fix: use the same predicate for the guard, e.g. `filter(|name| !normalize_catalog_key(name).is_empty())`.

**OK with notes.** The production change is correct, minimal, and its failure semantics (fatal `Config` for unresolvable, warning + `Ok(())` for an outage, one shared breaker/counters/summary path) are internally consistent and match the documented intent for the no-cache case. All findings are P2 report-only: two test-strength gaps, three stale doc/comment claims, one contrived edge case. Nothing blocks merge.

A walk-first regression is detectable because all three new ordering tests point `library.paths` at a non-existent root (`undiscoverable_library`, 7703-7710), so a walk-first run fails with `Scanner` instead of the asserted error.

**Finding: P2 — F8's artist-in-abort-message is unpinned.**
The four call sites are correct, but neither breaker test asserts the text: `discover_aborts_after_three_consecutive_provider_failures` (runner.rs:7354-7377) and `verify_named_artist_honours_the_provider_failure_limit` (7987-8041) check only `matches!(error, SeakarrError::MusicBrainz(_))`. For input `"'"` the message is `artist "'" is blank; …` (discover.rs:501-507), and the new test at runner.rs:7960-7970 encodes that wording by asserting `contains("is blank")`. The helper's own doc says the name “carries nothing to match on — blank, or made only of characters the catalogue key folds away”. Failure scenario: an operator typing a punctuation-only name is told it is blank, which does not explain the rejection. Smallest fix: say “is blank or contains nothing usable as an artist name” and update the assertion.

### Finding
- **Finding P2, doc-comment inaccuracy, `runner.rs:2571-2573`:** The comment says "Created before an explicitly named artist is verified, so a run that stops at that verification reports through the same counters and summary as one that walked the library." This is true for the `Stop` case (outage, not limit reached) where `finish_discover_run` is called, but NOT for the `unresolvable` case where the function returns `Err(SeakarrError::Config(...))` and the summary is NOT printed. The unresolvable case is already documented in the spec.
- **Finding P2, spec gap, `docs/agent/specs/2026-09-15-musicbrainz-library-gap-filling-design.md:520-522`:** The "Provider error, no cache" and "Three consecutive provider errors" entries in the Error handling section describe the automatic-sweep behavior ("skip and report the artist" / "abort the run with the failure"). For a named artist, the behavior is different (Stop with the artist name in the warning, or Err with the artist name in the abort message). The spec has a "Superseded on 2026-10-07" note only for the "Artist unresolved" entry at line 515-519; the other two entries need parallel notes. The README at line 1010-1015 covers this in prose, but the spec does not. Smallest fix: add two "Superseded on 2026-10-07" notes matching the pattern at line 515-519.
- **Finding P2, in-loop abort message uses on-disk spelling, `runner.rs:2702-2706, 2735-2739, 2778-2782`:** The pre-walk uses the typed name (`validated_filter` is the trimmed typed name, `runner.rs:2560-2562`), but the in-loop code uses `&artist.name`, which is the on-disk spelling for folder-only artists (set in `discover.rs:557` via `filter_folder`). If a stale-cache or provider-failure abort fires in the loop, the error message would say the on-disk name (e.g., "Shy Fx") instead of the typed name (e.g., "shy fx"). The pre-walk abort correctly uses the typed name (`runner.rs:2314`). The `discover_fills_an_artist_that_owns_a_folder_with_no_albums` test exercises this case but does not trigger an abort, so the discrepancy is not caught. Smallest fix: for the named-artist case, pass the typed name through to the in-loop abort (e.g., stash it in the `SelectedArtist` or in a separate variable) so the abort message always names what the operator typed.
- **Finding P2, test gap on error message, `runner.rs:7999-8004`:** The `verify_named_artist_honours_the_provider_failure_limit` test asserts `matches!(error, SeakarrError::MusicBrainz(_))` and the log substrings, but does not assert the error message content. The F8 fix added the artist name to the error message format `"{artist}: {DISCOVER_PROVIDER_FAILURE_LIMIT} consecutive MusicBrainz failures; aborting discover run"`. The warning and notice (which include the artist name) are pinned, but not the error message itself, so a regression that removed the artist from the error would not be caught. Smallest fix: add `assert!(error.to_string().contains("Breaker Named Artist"), ...)` to the test.
- **Finding P2, placeholder counter, `runner.rs:2573`:** `artists_total: usize::from(validated_filter.is_some())` initializes the counter to 1 for any named artist (even before the provider has been called) and is later overwritten by `selection.artists.len()` at `runner.rs:2643` only if the function reaches the walk. For the `Stop` case the placeholder survives and is used by `discover_notices` to suppress the "no eligible library artists" notice (`discover.rs:752`). This is semantically correct (a named artist counts as 1 work item even if it fails) but the placeholder-then-overwrite pattern is a bit unusual. Smallest fix: leave as-is; the comment at `runner.rs:2569-2573` already explains the rationale.

summary: no broad Soulseek artist search is issued and no folder-derived
discovery is attempted, so albums are never downloaded from an unverified

error naming the artist and no summary. `discography.artist_mbids` is the supported fix for a name MusicBrainz

the run instead, so a provider outage cannot grind through the rest of the
library.

## Summary of changes on branch main

- **The reported ordering problem is fixed.** `--mode discover --artist X` now asks MusicBrainz about `X` *before* `library.paths` is walked, and that answer is reused as the artist's work list — so one name costs exactly one MusicBrainz dialog. Previously the full tag-reading scan ran first and the verdict only arrived afterwards, wasting the scan when the artist was unverifiable.
- **Every failure mode now reports before the walk.** A name MusicBrainz cannot resolve is a hard configuration error raised without scanning; a provider outage warns, prints the run summary and ends the run before the walk (exit 0); a blank, whitespace-only or alias-only name is rejected before either — via a new `discover::validate_artist_filter` used by both the selection and the pre-walk gate. A compatible discography cache (fresh, or stale with a failed refresh) answers instead of stopping.
- **Scope respected.** The automatic sweep (no `--artist`) still derives its artist list from the scan, since its artist list *is* the scan's output; manual mode is untouched — its `--album` path never constructs a MusicBrainz provider, and artist-only manual keeps its legacy heuristic fallback.
- **Supporting fixes:** the breaker abort message now names the artist that tripped it; `discover_notices` no longer prints "no eligible library artists found; nothing to do" beside a failure notice; the counters/report/summary are created once so a pre-walk stop and a normal exit report identically; three stale comments/docs claiming the on-disk folder spelling is the MusicBrainz query were corrected to the operator's typed name driving the query and the on-disk spelling driving search/placement.
- **Documentation:** `README.md` (discover section, `--artist` row, three FAQ answers) and two design specs carry dated `2026-10-07` supersession notes for the changed ordering, the query spelling and the named-artist error contract.
- **Verification behind it:** 12 added/updated tests (ordering proven via a non-existent library root, hard error, outage stop, one-lookup reuse, fresh and stale cache paths, blank-name rejection, breaker abort text), project coverage **97.45% lines**, and clippy / fmt / tests / markdownlint / `cargo audit` / `cargo deny` / pre-commit all clean.

content.text:
Exploration done. What grounds this design:

- **The seam is small and already name-plumbed.** `--artist` is a single `Option<String>`; in discover it is resolved *before* the library walk (v0.31.0) through `discover_artist_albums` → `search_artists(name)` → `resolve_artist()` (exact-normalised-name match, then score-100/10-point dominance) → `release_groups(mbid)`.
- **A pinning mechanism already exists, but only in config:** `discography.artist_mbids` maps a typed name → hyphenated MusicBrainz UUID and bypasses the name search entirely (`artist_by_id`). The README's current advice for an unresolvable artist is "add the name and UUID to `discography.artist_mbids`". Your request is essentially that escape hatch, but on the command line and keyed by IPI/ISNI.
- **There is no IPI/ISNI awareness anywhere in the code today** (`rg -i 'isni|ipi' src/` finds nothing), and `ArtistWire` parses only `id`, `name`, `score` — so candidate *verification* against an identifier needs a small addition.
- **Live-verified against MusicBrainz just now:** `isni:0000000466597022` and `ipi:00581977202` both return exactly one artist — `Grafix`, MBID `c02a5966-b5c4-483a-8326-483edcf3680e`, score 100 — and the search response carries `"ipis":["00581977202"]` and `"isnis":["0000000466597022"]`, so a match can be confirmed from the artist's own identifiers rather than inferred from a score. (The spaced form you wrote also resolves; the plain MBID *lookup* endpoint does not expose `ipis`/`isnis`, only search does.)
- **Cache/failure keys are name-normalised** (`normalize_catalog_key`), and the discography cache row already stores `artist_mbid` with a compatibility check against a configured UUID — relevant to how an identifier run should cache.
- **Existing failure semantics to stay consistent with:** since v0.31.0 an explicitly named artist that MusicBrainz cannot resolve is a hard configuration error raised *before* the scan, and the automatic sweep is untouched.

First decision — the CLI surface, which everything else hangs off:

content.text:
One value only — that keeps the surface minimal.

Next, the case that actually decides correctness: an IPI or ISNI is not guaranteed unique in MusicBrainz (a person and a group, or merged/duplicate artist entries, can share one), unlike a UUID.

options.description: A code is only accepted when exactly one MusicBrainz artist both matches the search and actually carries that code in its own identifier list. Several artists sharing it is a hard error that names the count and the candidates and points at the UUID form of `--artist` (or `discography.artist_mbids`) as the precise escape hatch. Never guesses; consistent with the hard error an unresolvable name already raises before the scan.
options.label: Exactly one carrier, or refuse (Recommended)

options.description: Feed identifier matches through the existing resolver rules (score 100 with a 10-point lead over the runner-up) instead of demanding a single carrier. Reuses code already in place, but MusicBrainz scores identifier hits at or near 100 regardless of which artist it is, so ties are the norm and the practical result is almost always the same refusal — with a less honest error message.
options.label: Reuse the existing dominance rules

options.description: Take the highest-scoring identifier match and warn in the summary about the ones not chosen. Always completes a run and needs no user follow-up, but a shared IPI or ISNI means the wrong artist's discography can be downloaded into the wrong folder with only a warning standing between that and your library.
options.label: Pick the best match and warn

content.text:
## Design — identify a discover/manual artist by IPI, ISNI or MusicBrainz ID

This is a single-seam change (one flag's value parsing, one provider method, one resolver), so I'm presenting it in one pass with the sections marked; say which section you want revised and I'll iterate. Everything below is grounded in the live MusicBrainz probes and the code reads from this session.

### 1. CLI surface

`--artist` stays a single `Option<String>` and gains no new flags. The value's shape decides what it means:

| Shape (after stripping spaces/hyphens) | Treated as | Validation |
|---|---|---|
| `8-4-4-4-12` hex UUID | MusicBrainz artist ID | existing `valid_mbid` rules |
| 16 characters, digits with an optional trailing `X` | ISNI | ISO 7064 MOD 11-2 check digit verified |
| 11 digits | IPI | digits only |
| anything else | artist name | exactly today's behaviour |

A value that *looks* like a code but fails validation (wrong ISNI check digit, 15 digits, 12 digits) is a **configuration error naming the problem**, not a name search for a digit string. That is the only behaviour change for a name-shaped input.

### 2. Provider layer (`src/discography/`)

- New `ArtistIdentifier { Isni(String), Ipi(String) }`, stored normalised (digits, ISNI upper-case `X` preserved).
- New trait method `search_artists_by_identifier(&self, &ArtistIdentifier) -> Result<Vec<ArtistCandidate>, DiscographyError>`, building `isni:"…"` / `ipi:"…"` inside `musicbrainz.rs` and reusing the existing page-consistency checks verbatim.
- A UUID needs no search: it reuses `artist_by_id(mbid)`, which is an exact entity lookup and more reliable than an `arid:` query.
- `ArtistWire` gains `#[serde(default)] ipis`/`isnis` (and the optional `disambiguation`), so `ArtistCandidate` carries the identifiers a candidate actually claims. Cost: test fixtures constructing `ArtistCandidate` gain two empty vecs — mechanical.

### 3. Resolution

`resolve_artist_by_identifier(identifier, candidates)`:

- keep only candidates whose **own** identifier list contains the requested code (a fuzzy search hit that does not carry it is discarded — this is what makes the match exact rather than score-trusted);
- exactly one → resolved, recorded as a new `ArtistResolution::Identifier` variant;
- none → `ArtistUnresolved` with a reason naming the code;
- several → `ArtistUnresolved` with a reason naming the count and the candidate names/MBIDs, and pointing at the UUID form. No new error variant: "cannot resolve to exactly one artist" is already what that variant means, and the existing cache/breaker classification applies unchanged.

### 4. Data flow

`discover_artist_albums_at` keeps taking the raw string (so both callers and their tests are untouched at the signature level) and parses it once through a shared pure `parse_artist_input`. A code input:

1. keys the cache and the failure cache as `isni:<digits>` / `ipi:<digits>` (distinct from any name key, and distinct between the two kinds);
2. still honours a `discography.artist_mbids` pin keyed by that same string, which wins and skips the search — the documented escape hatch for a shared code;
3. resolves to a candidate, and **returns the canonical name** (today it is discarded; the cache row already stores it). In discover, that canonical name becomes the work item's name, so `ArtistFolderIndex` lookup, the Soulseek `Artist Album` search, placement and the processed records all follow today's rules — the on-disk folder spelling wins when the library holds one, staging plus the existing warning otherwise. Names behave exactly as now.
4. logs/summarises the resolution (`resolved ISNI … to Grafix (MBID …, "DnB producer Josh Jackson")`) so the operator sees which identity was picked.

### 5. Error handling and scope

- Discover: a code with no single carrier is the **same hard Config error raised before the library walk** that v0.31.0 introduced for unresolvable names. Provider errors keep their breaker classification.
- Artist-only manual: a code that resolves fetches as normal. **A code miss is a hard error, not the legacy folder heuristic fallback** — falling back would mean searching Soulseek for `0000000466597022`, which is the "fail late and confusingly" behaviour you rejected. *This is the one judgement call I'd like you to confirm.*
- `--mode manual --artist X --album Y` and `--batch-file` lines reject a recognisable identifier with a configuration error, because those paths never ask MusicBrainz and a code cannot name a folder.
- Out of scope: no scanner change (file tags carry no MusicBrainz IDs, so presence stays name-based), no new config keys, no identifiers in the automatic sweep or `discover.exclude_artists`, one identifier per run.

### 6. Testing and docs

Pure tests for the parser (each shape, spaced forms, bad ISNI check digit, digits-that-are-not-a-code) and for the resolver (one / none / several carriers, and a fuzzy hit that lacks the code); provider tests for query construction and `ipis`/`isnis` parsing; runner tests reusing the v0.31.0 non-existent-library-root technique to prove a code is verified before the walk and that the resolved canonical name drives search and placement; mode tests for the rejected paths; the existing name-path suite must pass unchanged. Docs: `--artist` row, the discover/ambiguity FAQs, the `artist_mbids` row, plus dated supersession notes in the two specs that state the artist-source contract. Expected version bump: MINOR.

# Artist identification by IPI, ISNI or MusicBrainz ID

## Problem

`--artist` accepts an artist name, and discovery resolves that name against
MusicBrainz: candidates must match the requested canonical name exactly, and
several exact-name matches are only accepted when one is uniquely dominant
(score 100 with a 10-point lead). A name MusicBrainz cannot tie to exactly one
artist therefore fails: in discover mode it is a configuration error raised
before the library walk, and in artist-only manual mode it falls back to the
legacy folder heuristic.

Some artists are identified far more reliably by their rights identifiers than by
their name. The motivating case is the drum-and-bass producer Grafix, whose
MusicBrainz record carries IPI `00581977202` and ISNI `0000 0004 6659 7022`; a
name search for `Grafix` competes with every other spelling and credit of that
name, while either code points at exactly one artist.

Today the only way to pin an identity is `discography.artist_mbids`, a
name-to-UUID map in `seakarr.yml`. That works, but it needs the hyphenated UUID
rather than the code the operator actually holds, requires editing configuration
before a one-off run, and keys on the name that failed to resolve in the first
place.

MusicBrainz supports both codes in artist search. Verified live on 2026-10-07:

- `query=isni:0000000466597022` returns exactly one artist, `Grafix`, MBID
  `c02a5966-b5c4-483a-8326-483edcf3680e`, score 100.
- `query=ipi:00581977202` returns the same single artist with score 100.
- The search response carries the candidate's own identifiers
  (`"ipis":["00581977202"]`, `"isnis":["0000000466597022"]`) and a
  `disambiguation` comment (`DnB producer Josh Jackson`), so a match can be
  confirmed from the artist's record rather than inferred from a relevance score.
- The plain entity lookup `/ws/2/artist/<mbid>` does **not** return `ipis` or
  `isnis`; only search does.

## Goal

Let `--artist` carry an exact MusicBrainz identity — an ISNI, an IPI, or an
artist UUID — and fetch that artist's discography without adding new flags,
without weakening name resolution, and without guessing when a code matches more
than one artist.

## Scope

**In scope**

- Value-shape detection on the existing `--artist` flag.
- A provider search path for IPI and ISNI; the existing MBID lookup for UUIDs.
- Strict single-carrier resolution with candidate self-verification.
- Discover mode and artist-only manual mode.
- The resolved canonical name as the work item's name.
- Cache keys, the `discography.artist_mbids` interaction, observability, docs.

**Out of scope**

- Reading MusicBrainz IDs from file tags. The library scanner captures artist,
  album and bitrate only, so presence, placement and the folder gate stay
  name-based; identity matching against the library is not part of this design.
- New configuration keys. `discography.artist_mbids` keeps UUID values; only its
  keys gain the ability to be a code.
- Identifiers in the automatic sweep or in `discover.exclude_artists`, which are
  library-derived and name-keyed.
- Identifiers in `--mode manual --album Y` runs and in `--batch-file` lines,
  which never ask MusicBrainz.
- Supplying more than one identifier for a single run.
- `arid:` search for UUIDs: an entity lookup already exists and is exact.

## Decisions

### The existing flag carries the identifier, and its shape decides

`--artist` stays a single `Option<String>`; no flag is added. Auto-detection was
chosen over explicit `--artist-ipi`/`--artist-isni` flags because the whole point
is to be simpler than editing configuration, and over a config-only extension
because a one-off run should not need a config edit. Accepted cost: a band
literally named like one of the code shapes would be read as a code. The escape
hatch is the existing `discography.artist_mbids` pin, which takes precedence over
the input's own shape (see Caching and pins).

### One value per run

Supplying a name *and* a code together is not supported: the code alone is
strictly more precise, so there is nothing to combine, and a precedence rule
would be one more thing to document, test and get wrong.

### Exactly one carrier, or refuse

A candidate counts only if its own `ipis`/`isnis` array contains the requested
code. Zero carriers and several carriers are both refusals, reported distinctly.
An IPI or ISNI is not unique by construction — a person and a group, or two
MusicBrainz entities for one act, can share one — and the existing dominance
rules cannot help because MusicBrainz scores identifier hits at or near 100
regardless of which artist they are. Refusing is also consistent with the hard
error an unresolvable name already raises before the walk.

### Codes are honoured where a discography is fetched

Discover mode and artist-only manual mode both accept a code, matching how
`discography.artist_mbids` already applies to both. Paths that never ask
MusicBrainz — `--mode manual --artist X --album Y` and batch lines — reject a
recognisable identifier with a configuration error, because a code cannot name a
library folder and searching Soulseek for a digit string fails late and
confusingly.

### A code-only run names the work item after the resolved artist

The work item carries the canonical MusicBrainz name of the artist that owns the
code. Library folder lookup, the `Artist Album` search, placement and the
processed records then follow today's rules unchanged: the on-disk folder
spelling wins when the library already holds a folder for that artist, otherwise
the existing staging fallback and warning apply. A code run behaves exactly like a
run naming that canonical name, except the identity came from the code.

### IPI and ISNI get a provider search; UUIDs reuse the entity lookup

A new `search_artists_by_identifier` covers IPI and ISNI, keeping MusicBrainz
query syntax inside the HTTP layer where it lives today. A UUID needs no search:
`artist_by_id` is an exact entity lookup and is more reliable than an `arid:`
query. The existing heavily tested `search_artists(name)` path is untouched.

## CLI surface

| `--artist` value, after stripping spaces and hyphens | Treated as | Validation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `8-4-4-4-12` hexadecimal UUID | MusicBrainz artist ID | the existing `valid_mbid` rules |
| 16 characters, digits with an optional trailing `X` | ISNI | ISO 7064 MOD 11-2 check digit |
| 11 digits | IPI | digits only; IPI has no check digit |
| anything else | artist name | today's behaviour, unchanged |

A value that looks like a code but fails validation — a bad ISNI check digit, 15
or 12 digits, a UUID with the wrong group lengths — is a configuration error
naming the problem. It is not silently searched for as a name, and it does not
claim the artist is unknown. This is the only change in behaviour for a
name-shaped input.

IPIs carry no check digit, so a mistyped but well-formed IPI surfaces as "no
MusicBrainz artist carries this IPI" rather than as a validation error.

## Provider layer

- `ArtistIdentifier { Isni(String), Ipi(String) }`, held normalised: digits only
  for both, with an ISNI check character upper-cased. Parsing and normalisation
  are pure functions shared by the CLI validation, the resolver and the cache key.
- `DiscographyProvider` gains
  `search_artists_by_identifier(&self, &ArtistIdentifier) -> Result<Vec<ArtistCandidate>, DiscographyError>`.
  The implementation builds `isni:"…"` or `ipi:"…"` and reuses the existing
  request, pacing, retry, `offset != 0` and count-versus-payload consistency
  checks verbatim, so an identifier search classifies its failures exactly as a
  name search does.
- `ArtistWire` gains `#[serde(default)] ipis`, `isnis` and `disambiguation`.
  `ArtistCandidate` gains the two identifier lists so the resolver can verify a
  candidate; `disambiguation` is carried for reporting.
- Test fixtures that construct `ArtistCandidate` gain two empty vectors. This is
  mechanical and is the accepted cost of keeping one candidate type rather than a
  parallel identifier-only type.

## Resolution

`resolve_artist_by_identifier(identifier, candidates)`:

1. Keep the candidates whose own identifier list contains the requested code,
   compared after normalisation.
2. Exactly one carrier resolves, recorded as a new `ArtistResolution::Identifier`
   variant so the log evidence distinguishes a code match from a name match.
3. No carrier is `DiscographyError::ArtistUnresolved` with a reason naming the
   code.
4. Several carriers is `DiscographyError::ArtistUnresolved` with a reason naming
   the count and the carriers, and pointing at the UUID form.

No new error variant is introduced: "cannot resolve to exactly one artist" is
what `ArtistUnresolved` already means, so the failure cache records it, the
circuit breaker does not count it, and discover raises its existing hard
configuration error before the library walk.

## Data flow

`discover_artist_albums_at` keeps its current signature and parses the artist
string once through the shared parser, so both callers and their test doubles are
unchanged at the call boundary.

For a code input:

1. The cache key is `isni:<digits>` or `ipi:<digits>` — prefixed so the two kinds
   cannot collide and so a code key cannot collide with a name key.
2. A `discography.artist_mbids` entry keyed by that same string wins and skips the
   search, exactly as a name-keyed pin does today.
3. Otherwise the provider is asked, and the resolver applies the single-carrier
   rule.
4. `discography_artist_albums` returns the resolved canonical name alongside the
   albums. Today that name reaches only the cache row and the debug log; it now
   also becomes the work item's name in the runner.
5. Discover's pre-walk verification (`verify_named_artist`) uses the canonical
   name for the selection and for `ArtistFolderIndex`, so placement follows the
   existing folder-spelling rules.
6. The resolution is logged and summarised: the code, the canonical name, the
   MBID and the disambiguation comment when MusicBrainz supplies one.

## Caching and pins

- The discography cache row keeps its existing shape; only the key can now be an
  identifier key. Rows still record `artist_mbid` and `canonical_artist`, and the
  compatibility check against a configured pin is unchanged.
- The failure cache records an identifier-keyed resolution failure under the same
  rules as a name-keyed one, so a repeated code run replays the recorded failure
  cheaply. An explicit `--artist` run bypasses the recorded failure, so a code run
  always asks once, matching the rule established for names.
- Consequence: a name run and a code run for the same artist keep separate cache
  rows and cost one extra release-group fetch the first time. This is accepted
  rather than solved, because keying by MBID would require a second cache lookup
  path and a schema change for a bounded, one-off cost.

## Error handling

| Situation | Discover | Artist-only manual | Album-only manual / batch |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Malformed code-shaped value | Configuration error at mode resolution, before any request | Same | Same |
| Code with exactly one carrier | Resolved before the walk; library scanned with the canonical name | Resolved; albums fetched | Rejected as a configuration error |
| Code with no carrier | Hard configuration error before the walk | **Hard configuration error**, not the legacy heuristic fallback | Rejected as a configuration error |
| Code with several carriers | Hard configuration error naming the count and the carriers | Same | Rejected as a configuration error |
| MusicBrainz unreachable | Existing breaker and skip behaviour | Existing fallback with its notice | Not applicable |

The manual-mode refusal is deliberate: the legacy heuristic exists to guess album
names for an artist that was named, and running it for a code would search
Soulseek for a digit string.

## Observability

One log line and one summary notice per identifier resolution, carrying the input
code, the resolved canonical name, the MBID and the disambiguation comment when
present. This is what lets an operator confirm that a shared IPI or ISNI picked
the artist they meant, and it is the only place the canonical-name decision
becomes visible.

## Components and boundaries

- `src/discography/identifier.rs` (new): `ArtistIdentifier`, `parse_artist_input`,
  normalisation, ISNI check digit, `resolve_artist_by_identifier`. Pure and
  free of I/O, so it is testable without a provider.
- `src/discography/mod.rs`: `discover_artist_albums_at` branches on the parsed
  input, keys the caches, consults the pin, and returns the canonical name;
  `ArtistResolution` gains `Identifier`; `ArtistCandidate` and the provider trait
  gain their fields and method.
- `src/discography/musicbrainz.rs`: query construction for `ipi:`/`isni:`, wire
  fields, and the identifier search implementation.
- `src/runner.rs`: `verify_named_artist` uses the canonical name for a code input
  when building the selection; the manual path refuses a code that resolves to
  nothing instead of falling back.
- `src/mode.rs`: rejects a recognisable identifier for album-only manual and batch
  inputs, using the same parser so the rule cannot drift.
- `src/main.rs`: `--artist` help text lists the accepted shapes.

## Testing

- **Parser**: each shape; spaced and hyphenated ISNI and IPI; lower-case ISNI
  check character; bad ISNI check digit; 15- and 17-character digit strings; UUID
  with wrong group lengths; a plain name containing digits; a name that is exactly
  11 digits is an IPI by design and is asserted as such.
- **Resolver**: one carrier resolves; a search hit that does not carry the code is
  discarded; no carrier and several carriers each produce `ArtistUnresolved` with
  their distinct reasons; comparison ignores spacing and ISNI case.
- **Provider**: the identifier query is escaped and encoded like the name query;
  `ipis`/`isnis`/`disambiguation` parse when present and default when absent.
- **Runner, discover**: a code is verified before the library walk, proven with the
  non-existent-library-root technique that pins ordering today; a code with no
  carrier is a hard error before the walk; the resolved canonical name drives the
  search and the placement folder.
- **Runner, artist-only manual**: a code fetches albums; a code with no carrier
  fails instead of using the heuristic.
- **Mode**: an identifier with `--album` and in a batch line is a configuration
  error.
- **Regression**: the whole existing name-path suite passes unchanged, and a
  name-shaped input behaves exactly as it does today.

## Documentation

- `README.md`: the `--artist` row and help text (four accepted shapes and their
  precedence), the discover and ambiguity FAQ entries, the `discography.artist_mbids`
  row (keys may be a code), and the resolution log line.
- Dated supersession notes in `docs/agent/specs/2026-09-15-musicbrainz-library-gap-filling-design.md`
  (artist source and `--artist` narrowing) and
  `docs/agent/specs/2026-09-13-dominant-musicbrainz-artist-resolution-design.md`
  (the name-only resolution contract now has an identity-based alternative).

## Accepted consequences

- A band named exactly like a code shape is read as a code; the config pin is the
  way out, and the parser is the single place to revisit that trade.
- Name runs and code runs for one artist keep separate cache rows.
- An IPI typo is not detected by validation, only by the empty result.
- Placement for a code run depends on the canonical name matching a library
  folder after normalisation; a differently spelled folder still falls back to
  staging with a warning, as it does today.
- No library-side identity matching: the presence check remains name-based.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `--artist 0000 0004 6659 7022` in discover mode fetches the discography of the
   single artist carrying that ISNI, before the library is walked.
2. `--artist 00581977202` resolves the same artist by IPI.
3. `--artist c02a5966-b5c4-483a-8326-483edcf3680e` resolves it by UUID without a
   search request.
4. A code with no carrier, and a code with several carriers, each fail with a
   configuration error in discover and in artist-only manual mode, before any
   library scan in discover, and never fall back to the legacy heuristic.
5. A code in `--mode manual --artist X --album Y` or in a batch line is a
   configuration error.
6. Every existing name-based test passes unchanged, and `cargo clippy`,
   `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo test`, the coverage floor and the markdown lint all
   pass.

content.text:
## Spec written and committed

**`docs/agent/specs/2026-10-07-artist-identifier-resolution-design.md`** — 318 lines, commit `f55607e` on `main` (committed locally; not pushed — the spec chain has no integration step).

It captures the decisions you made, each with its rationale and accepted cost:

| Decision | Rationale recorded |
|---|---|
| `--artist` keeps its shape as the discriminator (UUID / 16-char ISNI with check digit / 11-digit IPI / name) | No new flags; the only behaviour change for name-shaped input is that a malformed code is an error rather than a name search |
| One identity per run | A code is strictly more precise than a name, so there is nothing to combine |
| Exactly one candidate **whose own `ipis`/`isnis` array contains the code**, or refuse | An IPI/ISNI is not unique by construction, and MusicBrainz scores identifier hits at ~100 regardless of artist, so score dominance cannot decide |
| Codes honoured in discover and artist-only manual; rejected for `--album` runs and batch lines | Those paths never ask MusicBrainz and a code cannot name a library folder |
| A code-only run names the work item after the resolved canonical name | Library lookup, Soulseek search, placement and processed records then follow today's rules unchanged |
| New `search_artists_by_identifier` for IPI/ISNI; UUIDs reuse `artist_by_id` | Query syntax stays inside `musicbrainz.rs`; the tested name path is untouched |

**Self-review results:** no placeholders; three inconsistencies found and fixed (a wrong function name in the data-flow section; the manual-mode refusal now covers a provider outage as well as a code with no carrier — both would otherwise send a digit string to the Soulseek heuristic; and the canonical name's route out of the resolver is now pinned as a field on the outcome's authoritative variants rather than hand-waved). Scope is a single implementation plan, the one genuine ambiguity (an artist *named* like a code) is decided and recorded as an accepted consequence, prose is within the project's 120-character limit and `markdownlint` exits 0.

Worth flagging as the two things I decided rather than asked, both stated in the spec: the discography cache gains identifier keys (`isni:<digits>` / `ipi:<digits>`) so a name run and a code run for one artist cost one extra fetch the first time, and no library-side identity matching is attempted because the scanner reads no MusicBrainz IDs from tags.

## Tech Debt Remediation — complete

**Upstream Workflow Barrier:** read-only fleet check → no active runs. No live reviewer workflow, so remediation proceeded (no `REVIEW_GATE_STATUS` touched from this step).

**Step 0 routing:** `git diff --name-only HEAD` → 7 Rust files (`src/{config,main,mode,runner}.rs`, `src/discography/{identifier,mod,musicbrainz}.rs`) + 3 Markdown. `Cargo.toml` is present → **Common (Steps 1–5) + Rust**. No `*.py` changed → Python section skipped (not applicable, stated rather than skipped).

### Common Step 1 — redundant/overlapping tests
No tests removed. The 47 new tests each pin a distinct claim. One structural look-alike — `an_eleven_digit_value_is_an_ipi` (`00581977202`) and `a_band_named_like_a_code_shape_is_read_as_that_code` (`12345678901`) — asserts the same shape rule with a different literal; I kept both because the second is the only executable pin for the accepted "a band named like a code is read as that code" trade-off, so removing it would drop coverage of a documented consequence rather than remove noise.

### Common Step 2 + Rust Step 2 — coverage (measured fresh on the final tree)
`cargo llvm-cov -p seakarr --summary-only --fail-under-lines 95` → **exit 0**, **97.54% lines** (97.18% regions, 96.41% functions). The per-file check reports **no file below 95% lines**, including the new module (`discography/identifier.rs` 97.36%) and every changed file (config 96.58%, mod 98.62%, musicbrainz 97.10%, main 95.44%, mode 99.72%, runner 96.72%). No coverage remediation was needed, and no config, threshold or exclusion was touched.

### Rust Step 2b — cognitive-complexity gate (exact commands, no CRAP command invented)
`CLIPPY_CONF_DIR=/tmp/cx cargo clippy -p seakarr --lib -- -W clippy::cognitive-complexity` after `cargo clean -p seakarr` → 437 functions reported.

- **Ceiling (25):** no project function exceeds it. The only function above is `vendor/soulseek-rs-lib/src/client/operations.rs:12` (63) — the vendored third-party member you explicitly excluded from the ceiling earlier in this session (same file), so that recorded decision stands rather than being re-negotiated.
- **Triage bar (15):** 10 functions, all in files meeting the 95% coverage target, so the bar is satisfied: `src/download.rs:921` (25), `search.rs:924` (23), `client.rs:395` (23), `scanner.rs:261` (22), `filter.rs:1985` (21), **`runner.rs:2567` (20)**, `download.rs:1379` (20), `filter.rs:1879` (19), **`runner.rs:1954` (16)**, plus the vendored one. Reported explicitly because this change moved both runner entries: `run_discover_mode_with_provider` 18 → 20, and `run_artist_only_mode_with_provider` crossed from below 15 to 16 with the identifier refusal arms.

### Common Step 3 — full suite after the fixes
`cargo test -p seakarr` → **1005 + 39 + 13 + 3 + 4 + 0 tests, 0 failures**. No test was disabled, skipped or weakened.

### Common Step 4 — README accuracy
All changed non-doc files trigger a review (CLI entry point, config loading, public API modules, feature behaviour). One gap found and fixed: the `--artist` row documents the `--album` and batch rejections but not the rule that an identifier needs `discography.enabled: true` in artist-only manual mode, which was added after the documentation task ran — the FAQ bullet now states it. Verified as already accurate: the `artist_mbids` row (keys may be a name or `isni:<digits>`/`ipi:<digits>`, value always a UUID), the four `--artist` shapes, the canonical-name placement rule, and the resolution log line. `markdownlint README.md` → exit 0.

### Common Step 5a — docstring freshness audit (4 read-only subagents, all completed)
Batched across the 7 changed source files. The audits returned **20 unique findings**; I verified every one against the code before applying it:

- **18 were doc/comment corrections:** wrong pin-key form in the module doc (`ipi:12345678901`, not the bare digits), `parse`'s claim about validation, `display` claiming the operator's exact spelling, `validate` claiming `select_artists` applies the same rule, `label` returning `artist` not `name`, and the ISNI check-digit algorithm description (`12 - remainder`, not "final remainder is 1"); `select_albums`' `artist` parameter and three other `discography/mod.rs` docs that still spoke only of names (`is_stable_artist_resolution_failure`, `FailureCacheUse::Bypass`, `record_resolution_failure`), plus `Discovery`'s claim that the canonical name is absent from the variants; six `runner.rs` docs/comments saying "named" where the flow is now "targeted" (including the abort-message comment, which misdescribed which spelling it prints); and the `--artist` clap help, which stated the accepted shapes unconditionally.
- **2 were real behaviour bugs and were fixed in code, not prose.** My plan had name inputs follow the *resolved canonical MusicBrainz spelling* in both runner paths, which the approved spec scoped to code-only requests. That silently changed what a name-only run searches and places under (and could have bypassed discover's tag-vs-folder spelling rule for punctuation-variant names like `AC/DC`). `verify_named_artist` now uses the canonical name only for an identity and the operator's trimmed spelling for a name, and `run_artist_only_mode_with_provider` likewise.

### Common Step 5b — configuration staleness
The template `find` command returned **no results**. The bootstrap `seakarr.yml` is generated from code (`serde_yaml::to_string(&default_config)`), so no template can drift; per the Rust section's note I cross-checked the README's documented keys against the code defaults instead — no config key was added or renamed by this change, and the `artist_mbids` key semantics are documented and match the validator.
